set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: Which statement describes how Strongyloides stercoralis can reinfect the same host?
opts: Its larvae pass through a snail first

Passing through a snail is the rat lungworm's route, since snails are its intermediate hosts. Strongyloides needs no intermediate host: it completes its life cycle in humans or moist soil and can reinfect the same host without leaving the body.
Its eggs are swallowed in food or water

Swallowing mature eggs in contaminated food or water is how Ascaris lumbricoides is caught, its eggs spread by food, drink or contaminated objects. Strongyloides larvae instead penetrate the skin, and it can reinfect the same host without leaving the body.
It does so without leaving the body

Correct. Strongyloides stercoralis, the threadworm, can reinfect the same host without leaving the body. Its larvae normally penetrate the skin, migrate to the lungs, are swallowed and complete development in the intestine; heavy worm loads can cause pneumonitis, eosinophilia, bloody diarrhea and malabsorption.
Its eggs on the anal skin are swallowed

Eggs from the anal area picked up and swallowed are pinworm self-inoculation, after the females emerge to release eggs. Strongyloides goes further: it can reinfect the same host without leaving the body at all.

set1.q: Outside the intestine, which organ does Entamoeba histolytica invade most commonly?
opts: Lungs

The lungs can be infected (pulmonary amebiasis), but they are not the most common site. The organ amebas most commonly invade outside the intestine is the liver, where abscesses with active trophozoites cause amebic hepatitis.
Brain

The brain is on the list of organs Entamoeba histolytica can infect, yet it is not the most common; rapid brain destruction is the hallmark of Naegleria fowleri, which follows the olfactory nerve. The most common extraintestinal site is the liver.
Spleen

The spleen sits with the adrenals, kidneys, skin and brain among the other organs that can be infected. Extraintestinal amebiasis most commonly invades the liver; an enlarged spleen is a feature of African sleeping sickness and systemic leishmaniasis.
Liver

Correct. In extraintestinal amebiasis the amebas invade the viscera of the peritoneal cavity, most commonly the liver, where they produce abscesses with active trophozoites (amebic hepatitis). The lungs, spleen, adrenals, kidneys, skin and brain can also be infected.

mis.Lungs: possible site taken for the most common
mis.Spleen: possible site taken for the most common

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set1.q: What is a host in which a helminth undergoes no parasitic development called?
opts: A biological vector

Biological vectors are arthropods that transmit infectious microbes while feeding, such as the mosquitoes that carry Wuchereria; for filarial worms the vector is also the intermediate host. A host with no parasitic development is a transport host.
A transport host

Correct. A transport host experiences no parasitic development; it only carries the worm onward. Toxocara's paratenic hosts work this way: larvae sit in the tissues of animals such as waterfowl without growing, and a dog, cat or human that eats the undercooked meat is infected.
An intermediate host

Larval development does occur in the intermediate host, as in snails for the rat lungworm or the mosquito vector for Wuchereria bancrofti. A host in which the worm experiences no parasitic development at all is a transport host.
A definitive host

The definitive host is where the most development happens: adulthood and mating occur there, as in the dog for Toxocara canis. A host in which the worm does not develop is a transport host, the reverse case.

mis.An intermediate host: intermediate host confused with the transport host
mis.A biological vector: vector confused with the transport host

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: A person who often eats undercooked crustaceans is at risk for which parasite?
opts: Paragonimus westermani
Correct. The lung fluke Paragonimus westermani cycles between carnivorous animals, snails and crustaceans. Humans are infected by eating undercooked crustaceans, and the worms migrate to the lungs.
Opisthorchis sinensis

Opisthorchis sinensis, the Chinese liver fluke, is caught from inadequately cooked freshwater fish, hence the warning against freshwater sushi. Undercooked crustaceans are the source of the lung fluke, Paragonimus westermani.
Fasciola hepatica

Fasciola hepatica cycles between herbivores, snails and aquatic plants, and humans are infected by eating raw aquatic plants, not crustaceans. Undercooked crustaceans carry the lung fluke, Paragonimus westermani.
Taenia solium

Taenia solium, the pork tapeworm, reaches humans as cysts in undercooked pork or as embryonated eggs in contaminated food or water. Undercooked crustaceans are the source of the lung fluke, Paragonimus westermani.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: A lifelong resident of the southern United States who has never traveled abroad is diagnosed with Chagas disease. What best explains acquiring it at home?
opts: Spread of the tsetse fly vector

The tsetse fly is the vector of Trypanosoma brucei and African sleeping sickness in West and East Africa, not of Chagas disease. The migrating vector behind Chagas disease in the southern United States is the reduviid bug.
Dogs serving as alternate hosts

Dogs are the alternate hosts of Leishmania in equatorial regions, where female sand flies spread it. Chagas disease in the southern United States is explained by migration of its own vector, the reduviid bug.
Lake water entering the nose

Water entering the nose transmits Naegleria fowleri and causes meningoencephalitis, not Chagas disease. Trypanosoma cruzi enters through reduviid bug feces, and that vector's migration explains cases in the southern United States.
Range expansion of its vector

Correct. Chagas disease was a tropical disorder of Latin America, but it is becoming an issue in the southern United States as its vector, the reduviid (kissing) bug, expands its range. Many now consider it endemic in the United States, so a case can be acquired without travel.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: Which group is advised not to clean a cat's litter box because of Toxoplasma gondii?
opts: Pregnant women

Correct. Cats harbor Toxoplasma oocysts and release them in their feces, and a pregnant woman who acquires toxoplasmosis can transmit it across the placenta to her fetus. So pregnant women should not clean the cat box, because of the danger of transplacental transmission.
Contact lens wearers

Contact lens wearers are the group at risk for amebic keratitis from Acanthamoeba, which lives in freshwater lakes, hot tubs and swimming pools. The cat box warning concerns Toxoplasma and pregnant women, because the parasite can cross the placenta.
Children in daycare

Daycare is the classic setting for pinworm, Enterobius vermicularis, spread by direct contact and fomites. The advice to avoid cleaning the cat box is aimed at pregnant women, since Toxoplasma from cat feces can pass across the placenta to the fetus.
People without a spleen

People without a spleen face serious babesiosis, a tick-borne infection of red blood cells by Babesia microti. The cat box warning is for pregnant women, because Toxoplasma shed in cat feces can be transmitted across the placenta.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: How do humans acquire Taenia saginata?
opts: Eating raw beef holding encysted larvae

Correct. Taenia saginata is the beef tapeworm, and humans are its definitive host. Infection occurs from eating raw beef in which the larval form has encysted; in the human, the larva attaches to the small intestine and becomes an adult.
Swallowing eggs from feces-tainted land

Grazing on land contaminated with human feces is how cattle, the intermediate host, become infected, not how humans do. Humans, the definitive host, acquire the beef tapeworm by eating raw beef in which the larval form has encysted.
Eating cysts in undercooked pork

Cysts in undercooked pork transmit the pork tapeworm, Taenia solium, causing taeniasis. Taenia saginata is the beef tapeworm, acquired from raw beef in which the larval form has encysted; cattle, not swine, are its intermediate host.
Handling dogs that carry the worm

Handling dogs who have the infection is how people typically acquire Echinococcus, a tiny tapeworm found in dogs. Taenia saginata uses humans as the definitive host and cattle as the intermediate host, so infection comes from raw beef.

mis.Swallowing eggs from feces-tainted land: the intermediate host's route given to humans

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set1.q: What produces the regular episodes of chills, fever and sweating in malaria?
opts: Shifting surface antigens

Changing surface antigens (antigenic variation) is how Trypanosoma brucei evades the immune response in African sleeping sickness. Malaria's regular chills-fever-sweating episodes follow the cycle of red blood cells rupturing and releasing merozoites.
Infected red blood cells bursting

Correct. In the erythrocytic phase, merozoites enter red blood cells, become ring trophozoites and multiply until the cell bursts and releases more merozoites. The symptoms recur at intervals as the red blood cells rupture, and the interval depends on the species.
Sporozoites dividing in the liver

Schizogony in the liver is the exoerythrocytic phase: it comes first and generates the merozoites that later enter the circulation. The recurring chills, fever and sweating are timed to red blood cells rupturing, not to the liver stage.
Gametes fusing in the bloodstream

Gametes do not fuse in the human: merozoites differentiate into gametes in the blood, but fertilization happens in the mosquito after it draws infected red blood cells. The cyclic symptoms come from red blood cells rupturing in the human host.

mis.Gametes fusing in the bloodstream: sexual phase placed in the human host

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set1.q: Where are the cysts of cysticercosis most damaging?
opts: Bile duct, gallbladder or pancreas

Inflammation or blockage of the bile duct, gallbladder or pancreas is the chronic phase of fascioliasis, from the liver fluke Fasciola hepatica. The cysts of cysticercosis are most damaging in heart muscle, eye or brain.
The spleen and the bladder

Enlargement and inflammation of the liver, spleen and bladder are signs of schistosomiasis, a blood fluke disease of the veins of the bowel or bladder. The cysts of cysticercosis, the encysted larvae of the pork tapeworm, are most damaging in heart muscle, eye or brain.
Heart muscle, eye or brain

Correct. In cysticercosis, eggs hatch in the intestine and release larvae that migrate to all tissues and encyst. The cysts are most damaging if they lodge in heart muscle, eye or brain, and in the brain they may cause seizures and psychiatric disturbances.
The liver and the lungs

Slowly enlarging cysts in the liver and lungs are cystic echinococcosis (hydatid disease), from the tiny tapeworm Echinococcus. Pork tapeworm larvae can encyst in any tissue, but their cysts do the most damage in heart muscle, eye or brain.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set1.q: Which measure prevents amebiasis caused by Entamoeba histolytica?
opts: Cooking pork thoroughly

Thorough cooking of pork guards against Trichinella spiralis, which is acquired from undercooked pork or bear meat. Amebiasis comes from swallowed Entamoeba cysts, with epidemics where water supplies are polluted, so water treatment is its prevention.
Controlling freshwater snails
Snail control prevents schistosomiasis, whose larvae develop in freshwater snails. Entamoeba histolytica has no snail stage: its cysts are swallowed, and water treatment is the prevention.
Treating the water supply

Correct. Water treatment is the prevention for amebiasis (a vaccine is under development). Entamoeba histolytica cysts are swallowed, and epidemics occur in concentrated populations where water supplies are polluted, such as prisons, hospitals and juvenile care institutions.
Using nose plugs when swimming

Nose plugs prevent primary amebic meningoencephalitis, because Naegleria fowleri burrows through the nasal mucosa from freshwater. Entamoeba histolytica is swallowed as cysts, and its prevention is water treatment.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: Giardiasis is common in campers. How is Giardia lamblia usually acquired?
opts: Water splashing up into the nose

Water entering the nose is how Naegleria fowleri is acquired from lakes and streams, reaching the brain along the olfactory nerve. Giardia lamblia is swallowed instead: its cysts are usually ingested with water and food.
Bites of blood-sucking insects

Blood-sucking insects spread the hemoflagellates, Trypanosoma and Leishmania, which live in the blood and tissues. Giardia lamblia is an intestinal flagellate whose cysts are ingested with water and food.
Handling infected farm pigs

Pigs are the hosts of Balantidium coli, the intestinal ciliate, and even that organism is acquired by ingesting cyst-containing food or water. Giardia lamblia reaches people the same way, as cysts ingested with water and food.
Swallowed cysts in water or food

Correct. Giardia lamblia cysts, small, compact and multinucleate, survive in the environment and are usually ingested with water and food; giardiasis is common in campers. The cysts enter the duodenum, germinate, and the trophozoites feed and multiply in the jejunum. Boiling, ozone and iodine kill the agent.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set1.q: Which measure controls both African sleeping sickness and Chagas disease?
opts: Controlling the insect vector

Correct. African sleeping sickness is spread by tsetse flies, and its control involves eliminating the tsetse fly. Chagas disease is spread by the reduviid bug, and its control is through control of the vector; a Chagas vaccine is still under development.
Avoiding undercooked meat

Avoiding undercooked meat guards against meat-borne parasites such as Trichinella spiralis and Sarcocystis. The trypanosomes reach people through insects, the tsetse fly and the reduviid bug, so both diseases are controlled by controlling the vector.
Controlling freshwater snails

Snail control prevents schistosomiasis, whose larvae develop in freshwater snails. The trypanosomes have no snail stage: they are carried by the tsetse fly and the reduviid bug, so control is aimed at the vector.
Washing fruits and vegetables

Washing produce, with snail and slug control, prevents rat lungworm (Angiostrongylus cantonensis). The trypanosomes are carried by blood-sucking insects, so African sleeping sickness and Chagas disease are controlled through the vector.
set1.cite: Lecture 16 Dr. Webster Parasites of Medical Importance.pptx, Slide 42, 45, 47, 49, 51, 71, 99, 101, 112 and 113

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set1.q: A previously healthy person develops headache, fever, vomiting and a stiff neck a few days after jet skiing on a lake, then becomes confused and starts hallucinating. How does this infection typically progress?
opts: Brain symptoms only years later

Brain symptoms years later mark the chronic Gambian form of African sleeping sickness, spread by tsetse flies. This patient's brain disease arrived within days of lake water exposure, the rapid destruction typical of Naegleria fowleri.
Chronic heart and brain inflammation

Chronic inflammation of organs, especially the heart and brain, is the long-term picture of Chagas disease from Trypanosoma cruzi. Meningitis signs and hallucinations days after lake water exposure follow the rapid destruction of Naegleria fowleri.
Rapid brain destruction and death

Correct. Headache, fever, vomiting and stiff neck after lake water contact, then confusion and hallucinations, is Naegleria meningoencephalitis. It causes rapid destruction of the brain and spinal cord, with lack of balance, coma and death, and its treatment must be early.
Meningitis with a longer progression

Symptoms of meningitis with a longer progression describe granulomatous amebic encephalitis from Acanthamoeba, which enters through broken skin or the nasal passages. Jet skiing followed within days by confusion and hallucinations fits the rapid destruction of Naegleria.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set1.q: A young, sexually active woman has a foul-smelling, green-to-yellow vaginal discharge, vulvitis, and urinary frequency with pain. How is the suspected protozoan diagnosed?
opts: Examination of a fecal smear

A fecal smear, with history and an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay using monoclonal antibodies, diagnoses Entamoeba histolytica, an intestinal ameba. Vaginal discharge with vulvitis points to Trichomonas vaginalis, found by microscopy of a vaginal smear.
Card agglutination test

The card agglutination test for trypanosomes gives rapid diagnosis of African sleeping sickness, spread by tsetse flies. This patient's genital symptoms point to Trichomonas vaginalis, diagnosed on a vaginal smear under the microscope.
Polymerase chain reaction of stool

Polymerase chain reaction is used for Giardia lamblia, because microscopy is difficult when the organism is shed in feces intermittently. A genital infection with this discharge is Trichomonas vaginalis, seen directly on a vaginal smear.
Microscopy of a vaginal smear

Correct. Foul-smelling, green-to-yellow discharge with vulvitis and painful, frequent urination in a young, sexually active woman points to trichomoniasis, the most common curable sexually transmitted disease in this group. Trichomonas vaginalis is diagnosed by microscopic analysis of a vaginal smear.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: How do humans acquire Opisthorchis sinensis, the Chinese liver fluke?
opts: Eating undercooked freshwater fish

Correct. The Chinese liver fluke cycles between mammals, snails and fish, and humans are infected by eating inadequately cooked fish that carry its larvae; hence the warning not to eat freshwater sushi. Its eggs leave in the feces, reach water and infect snails.
Eating undercooked freshwater crabs

Undercooked crabs and other crustaceans transmit the lung fluke, Paragonimus westermani, whose worms migrate to the lungs. The Chinese liver fluke reaches humans in inadequately cooked fish instead, as in freshwater sushi.
Eating raw aquatic plants

Raw aquatic plants transmit Fasciola hepatica, which cycles between herbivores, snails and aquatic plants and lodges in the liver. The Chinese liver fluke is caught from inadequately cooked freshwater fish, which carry its larvae.
Eating raw or undercooked pork

Raw or undercooked pork transmits the pork tapeworm, Taenia solium, causing taeniasis. The Chinese liver fluke is a fluke whose larvae reach humans in inadequately cooked freshwater fish, not in meat from swine.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: Cattle and pigs pick up Sarcocystis cysts while grazing on grass contaminated with human feces, and people are infected by eating their undercooked meat. What role do these animals play in the parasite's life cycle?
opts: Transport hosts

A transport host experiences no parasitic development and simply carries a parasite on toward its definitive host. Cattle and pigs are called the intermediate hosts of Sarcocystis: they acquire infective cysts while grazing, and people catch it from their undercooked meat.
Dead-end hosts

It is humans, not the grazing animals, who can be dead-end hosts for other Sarcocystis species, and then they develop muscle cysts, myalgia, weakness and edema. Cattle and pigs are the intermediate hosts whose undercooked meat infects people.
Intermediate hosts

Correct. For Sarcocystis, domestic animals are the intermediate hosts: they pick up infective cysts while grazing on grass contaminated with human feces, and humans are infected when the undercooked meat is eaten. Sarcocystis hominis comes from cattle and Sarcocystis suihominis from pigs.
Definitive hosts

The definitive host is where adulthood and mating occur. The grazing cattle and pigs are named the intermediate hosts of Sarcocystis: they pick up the cysts from contaminated grass and pass the infection on to people in their meat.
set1.cite: Lecture 16 Dr. Webster Parasites of Medical Importance.pptx, Slide 71, 79 and 108

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: How do people typically acquire Echinococcus?
opts: Being bitten by fleas

Fleas feed on warm-blooded animals and carry the zoonotic diseases plague and murine typhus. Echinococcus is instead acquired by handling dogs who have the infection, most often where dogs mix with sheep, cattle, goats or pigs.
Eating undercooked crabs
Undercooked crabs and other crustaceans transmit the lung fluke, Paragonimus westermani. Echinococcus is a tiny tapeworm that people typically acquire by handling dogs who have the infection.
Handling infected dogs

Correct. People typically acquire echinococcosis by handling dogs who have the infection; these tiny tapeworms are found in dogs. The disease is most prevalent where dogs interact with the intermediate hosts: sheep, cattle, goats and pigs.
Eating undercooked pork

Undercooked or raw pork transmits the pork tapeworm, Taenia solium, causing taeniasis. Pigs are only intermediate hosts of Echinococcus; people typically acquire it by handling dogs who have the infection.

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set1.q: Adult Toxocara canis worms live and mate in the small intestine of a dog. What is the dog's role in this worm's life cycle?
opts: Intermediate host

An intermediate host is where larval development takes place, as snails are for the rat lungworm. A dog carrying adult worms that mate in its intestine is where the cycle reaches adulthood, which makes it the definitive host.
Paratenic host

A paratenic host is a transport host in which the worm does not grow; for Toxocara these are animals such as waterfowl whose tissues hold larvae until a dog or cat eats them. The dog, holding adults that mate, is the definitive host.
Accidental host

Accidental host is the role of humans, who swallow infective eggs from feces or eat undercooked meat of a paratenic host; the larvae then migrate through human tissues. Adults that live and mate in a dog's intestine make the dog the definitive host.
Definitive host

Correct. Adulthood and mating occur in the definitive host, and adult Toxocara live in the small intestine of the dog (Toxocara canis) or the cat (Toxocara cati), which pass the eggs in their feces. Humans, by contrast, are accidental hosts, infected by swallowing those eggs.

mis.Intermediate host: larval host confused with the adult host
mis.Paratenic host: transport host confused with the definitive host
mis.Accidental host: human role assigned to the dog

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: How is Onchocerca volvulus, the cause of river blindness, transmitted?
opts: By the bite of black flies

Correct. Onchocerca volvulus is transmitted by biting black flies, which act as both vector and intermediate host. Larvae develop into adults in subcutaneous tissues, adult females migrate via the blood to the eyes, and coinfection with Wolbachia bacteria causes river blindness.
By the bite of mosquitoes

Mosquitoes spread a different tissue nematode, Wuchereria bancrofti, whose adults develop in the lymphatics and cause elephantiasis. River blindness is spread by black flies, its vector and intermediate host.
By the bite of tsetse flies

Tsetse flies spread Trypanosoma brucei, the protozoan of African sleeping sickness, which is controlled by eliminating the tsetse fly. River blindness is a filarial worm infection spread by biting black flies, its vector and intermediate host.
By the bite of deer ticks

The blacklegged deer tick, an arachnid, carries Babesia microti, a protozoan that attacks red blood cells in babesiosis. River blindness is a filarial worm infection carried by biting black flies, its vector and intermediate host.
set1.cite: Lecture 16 Dr. Webster Parasites of Medical Importance.pptx, Slide 8, 45, 47, 77, 104 and 106

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set1.q: Which is one way helminths cause disease in their human hosts?
opts: Provoking immune attack on their cuticle

The cuticle is one of the worms' adaptations to parasitism: it protects them against immune defense rather than drawing an attack. The damage comes from worms feeding on and migrating through tissues, accumulating in organs and causing blockages, and from toxic worm secretions.
Multiplying inside red blood cells

Multiplying inside red blood cells is how malaria parasites do harm: merozoites enter red cells, multiply and burst them, and Babesia also attacks red blood cells. Helminths are large multicellular animals whose damage comes from feeding on and migrating through tissues, blockages and toxic secretions.
Growing within the host cells they infect

Living inside host cells describes intracellular protozoa such as Plasmodium, an obligate intracellular sporozoan. Adult helminths are large multicellular animals with specialized tissues and organs; their pathology comes from feeding on and migrating through tissues, accumulating in organs and toxic secretions.
Feeding on and migrating through tissues

Correct. Helminth pathology arises from worms feeding on and migrating through tissues, from the accumulation of worms in organs, causing blockages, and from toxic worm secretions. The effects are enlargement and swelling of organs, hemorrhage, weight loss and anemia.

mis.Provoking immune attack on their cuticle: an adaptation read as the source of pathology

set1.cite: Lecture 16 Dr. Webster Parasites of Medical Importance.pptx, Slide 56, 58, 77, 79 and 85

set1.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set1.q: Which drawback do antiprotozoan drugs share as a group?
opts: Loss of effect from antigenic variation

Antigenic variation is how Trypanosoma brucei evades the host's immune response; it describes the parasite against immunity, not a property of the drugs. Antiprotozoan drugs as a group carry toxicity problems and severe side effects.
Toxicity and severe side effects

Correct. Antiprotozoan drugs have toxicity problems and severe side effects. They work against eukaryotic cells (protozoa are eukaryotic parasites), and they are relatively few in comparison with antibacterial agents, so both their number and their safety are limited.
No activity against eukaryotic cells

This reverses a defining feature: antiprotozoan drugs work against eukaryotic cells, which is what protozoa, single-celled animal-like microbes, are. The drawback they share is toxicity problems and severe side effects.
Resistance in most protozoan strains

Drug resistance is noted for particular organisms (increasing in malaria, a small share of Trichomonas strains), not as a trait of protozoa in general. What antiprotozoan drugs share as a group is toxicity problems with severe side effects, and they are relatively few in number.

mis.Loss of effect from antigenic variation: immune evasion confused with drug failure

set1.cite: Lecture 16 Dr. Webster Parasites of Medical Importance.pptx, Slide 9, 12, 14, 38, 46 and 61

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: By which route is Isospora belli transmitted to humans?
opts: The bite of a blacklegged deer tick

The blacklegged deer tick carries Babesia microti, a parasite that attacks red blood cells. Isospora belli is an intracellular intestinal parasite, transmitted in fecally contaminated food or drink and causing diarrhea, fatty stools and weight loss.
Undercooked beef or pork

Undercooked beef or pork is the source of Sarcocystis hominis and Sarcocystis suihominis, whose cysts the grazing cattle and pigs carry in their meat. Isospora belli is transmitted in fecally contaminated food or drink.
Sexual contact with a partner

Sexual contact transmits Trichomonas vaginalis, whose reservoir is the human urogenital tract; it causes the most common curable sexually transmitted disease in young women. Isospora belli is an intestinal parasite carried in fecally contaminated food or drink.
Fecally contaminated food or drink

Correct. Isospora belli, an intracellular intestinal parasite with an oocyst stage, is transmitted in fecally contaminated food or drink. Infection is usually asymptomatic or self-limited and is primarily associated with immunocompromised hosts.
set1.cite: Lecture 16 Dr. Webster Parasites of Medical Importance.pptx, Slide 74, 77, 71 and 37

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: What is the only host of the whipworm, Trichuris trichiura?
opts: Humans

Correct. Humans are the sole host of the whipworm. Its eggs, spread by fecal pollution of soil, are swallowed and hatch in the intestine, where the larvae attach, penetrate the outer wall and develop into adults. Trichuriasis has its highest incidence in the tropics, and in the United States in the South.
Pigs and wild mammals

Pigs and wild mammals are the life-cycle requirement of Trichinella spiralis, caught from undercooked pork or bear meat. The whipworm needs no animal at all: humans are its sole host, infected by swallowing eggs from soil polluted with human feces.
Dogs and cats

Dogs and cats are the definitive hosts of Toxocara canis and cati, the dog and cat roundworms, with humans as accidental hosts. Trichuris trichiura has no animal host; humans are its sole host, and its eggs reach people from fecally polluted soil.
Freshwater snails

Freshwater snails are intermediate hosts for the blood flukes and for the rat lungworm, Angiostrongylus cantonensis. The whipworm has no intermediate host: humans are its sole host, and its eggs are swallowed directly.

set1.q: Which form of leishmaniasis is the most severe and fatal if untreated?
opts: Primary chancre

A primary chancre is the skin lesion where a tsetse fly inoculates Trypanosoma brucei, not a form of leishmaniasis. Among the forms of leishmaniasis, kala azar is the most severe and fatal if untreated.
Kala azar

Correct. Leishmaniasis takes cutaneous, mucous membrane and systemic (visceral) forms, and kala azar is the most severe form, fatal if untreated. The cutaneous oriental sore, or Baghdad boil, is a localized ulcerated sore, and espundia is a chronic infection of the head.
Baghdad boil

The Baghdad boil, or oriental sore, is the cutaneous form, a localized ulcerated sore that arises when the infected macrophage does not migrate. The most severe form, fatal if untreated, is kala azar.
Espundia
Espundia is a chronic skin and mucous membrane infection of the head that occurs after the cutaneous form; it is not the most severe form. Kala azar is the most severe form and fatal if untreated.

mis.Baghdad boil: localized form taken for the severe one
mis.Espundia: chronic form taken for the fatal one

set1.q: Which worm disease is the most common among children in temperate zones?
opts: Toxocariasis (dog roundworm)

Toxocariasis, from the dog and cat roundworms, is one of the neglected parasitic infections named by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, with humans as accidental hosts. The most common worm disease of children in temperate zones is enterobiasis.
Enterobiasis (pinworm)

Correct. Enterobiasis, the pinworm or seatworm infection, is the most common worm disease of children in temperate zones. It is very common in daycare, spreading by direct contact and fomites; swallowed eggs hatch in the small intestine, and females emerge to release eggs, causing anal itching.
Trichuriasis (whipworm)

Trichuriasis has its highest incidence in the tropics, and in the United States in the South; heavy infestations can be fatal in children. The most common worm disease of children in temperate zones is enterobiasis, the pinworm or seatworm infection.
Ascariasis (roundworm)

Ascariasis, from the large intestinal roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides, has most United States cases in the southeastern states. The most common worm disease of children in temperate zones is enterobiasis, very common in daycare settings.

mis.Trichuriasis (whipworm): tropical worm placed in temperate zones

set1.q: Which finding distinguishes rat lungworm meningitis from bacterial meningitis?
opts: Encysted larvae on muscle biopsy

Coiled larvae encysted in skeletal muscle are found on biopsy in trichinellosis, from undercooked pork or bear meat. Rat lungworm infection is a meningitis, recognized by elevated eosinophils instead of neutrophils on lumbar puncture.
Eosinophils on lumbar puncture

Correct. Angiostrongylus cantonensis produces the symptoms of bacterial meningitis (nausea, vomiting, headaches, stiff neck), but the lumbar puncture shows elevated eosinophils instead of neutrophils. That is why the disease is called eosinophilic meningitis; eosinophils are the defense against worms.
Neutrophils on lumbar puncture

Neutrophils are what the lumbar puncture would show in bacterial meningitis; in the rat lungworm infection they are replaced by elevated eosinophils. Choosing neutrophils reverses the distinguishing finding.
Headache, stiff neck and vomiting

Nausea, vomiting, headaches and a stiff neck are shared: the rat lungworm produces the symptoms of bacterial meningitis, so they cannot separate the two. The lumbar puncture separates them, showing eosinophils instead of neutrophils.

set1.q: A swimmer develops diarrhea, vomiting and abdominal cramps after swimming in a properly chlorinated public pool. Which protozoan is the most likely cause?
opts: Balantidium coli

Balantidium coli does cause diarrhea and abdominal pain, but it comes from the intestines of pigs and cattle in cyst-containing food or water, and healthy humans are resistant. Illness after a chlorinated pool fits Cryptosporidium, which tolerates chlorine.
Cryptosporidium

Correct. Cryptosporidium is the leading cause of recreational waterborne disease and can tolerate the chlorine in swimming pools. Swallowed oocysts release sporozoites that penetrate intestinal cells, causing gastroenteritis with headache, sweating, vomiting, abdominal cramps and diarrhea.
Naegleria fowleri

Naegleria fowleri inhabits unchlorinated pools, lakes and hot springs, enters through the nose and destroys the brain and spinal cord, with headache, fever, vomiting and a stiff neck. A chlorinated pool and gastroenteritis point to Cryptosporidium, which tolerates chlorine.
Acanthamoeba

Acanthamoeba lives in swimming pools, hot tubs and freshwater lakes, but its diseases are amebic keratitis in contact lens wearers and granulomatous amebic encephalitis. Vomiting, cramps and diarrhea after pool water fit Cryptosporidium, which tolerates chlorine.

mis.Acanthamoeba: pool organism with eye or brain disease

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: Apart from the bite of its insect vector, by which route can a person acquire Plasmodium?
opts: Receiving a blood transfusion

Correct. Besides the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito, its primary vector, Plasmodium is transmitted by blood transfusions and from mother to fetus. That fits a parasite whose erythrocytic phase lives inside red blood cells, where merozoites become ring trophozoites and multiply.
Eating undercooked meat

Undercooked meat is how people acquire Sarcocystis from cattle or pigs, and raw meat is one way they acquire Toxoplasma, whose pseudocysts sit in the muscle of food animals. Plasmodium is a blood parasite passed by blood transfusion and from mother to fetus.
Nasal contact with lake water

Nasal contact with fresh water is the route of Naegleria fowleri, whose trophozoite burrows through the nasal mucosa and follows the olfactory nerve into the brain. Plasmodium lives in the blood, so apart from the mosquito it spreads by blood transfusion and from mother to fetus.
Swallowing oocysts in pool water

Swallowing oocysts in recreational water is how Cryptosporidium spreads, since it can tolerate chlorine in swimming pools. Plasmodium is a blood parasite: besides the mosquito's bite, it passes by blood transfusion and from mother to fetus.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set1.q: Which diseases do fleas carry as they feed on warm-blooded animals?
opts: Malaria and filariasis

Malaria and filariasis are transmitted by mosquitoes, whose females take the blood meal; mosquitoes require an aquatic habitat. Fleas, with their flattened bodies, carry the zoonotic diseases plague and murine typhus.
Lyme disease and tularemia

Lyme disease and tularemia are carried by hard (ixodid) ticks, arachnids that cling on vegetation and attach to a host on contact. Fleas are insects that carry the zoonotic diseases plague and murine typhus.
Plague and murine typhus

Correct. Fleas are highly motile insects with flattened bodies that feed on warm-blooded animals and carry zoonotic diseases: plague and murine typhus. Like other arthropods of medical importance, they transmit the microbes in the process of feeding, which makes them biological vectors.
Epidemic typhus and relapsing fever

Epidemic typhus and relapsing fever are spread by lice, which feed on blood and tissue fluid in head and body hair and release feces that contaminate the wound. The typhus that fleas carry is murine typhus, along with plague.

set1.q: As Trypanosoma brucei multiplies in the blood, which organs does it damage?
opts: Liver, lungs and adrenals

The liver, lungs and adrenals are among the viscera Entamoeba histolytica can invade in extraintestinal amebiasis, the liver most commonly. Trypanosoma brucei multiplies in the blood and damages the spleen, lymph nodes and brain.
Duodenum and jejunum

Giardia lamblia germinates in the duodenum and feeds and multiplies in the jejunum, causing diarrhea and abdominal pain. Trypanosoma brucei is a blood parasite that damages the spleen, lymph nodes and brain.
Spleen, lymph nodes and brain

Correct. After the bite, Trypanosoma brucei migrates into the lymphatics, disseminates in the blood, multiplies there and damages the spleen, lymph nodes and brain. Early fever, enlarged spleen and swollen lymph nodes give way to personality and behavioral changes, then sleep disturbances, seizures and coma.
Heart muscle and large intestine

The heart muscle and large intestine harbor masses of Trypanosoma cruzi in Chagas disease, with chronic inflammation especially of the heart. Trypanosoma brucei, the African trypanosome, damages the spleen, lymph nodes and brain.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set2.q: The pictured mouth is at the head end of a small intestinal worm. How do humans acquire this worm?
opts: Eating meat with larvae encysted in it

Meat holding encysted larvae transmits Trichinella spiralis, from undercooked pork or bear meat. The hookworm shown, with its hooked mouth, lives in the small intestine and is acquired when soil larvae burrow into bare skin.
The bite of a mosquito carrying larvae

Mosquito bites deposit the larvae of Wuchereria bancrofti, a tissue nematode that develops in the lymphatics. The hooked-mouth worm pictured is an intestinal hookworm, transmitted through the skin on the soles of the feet.
Larvae burrowing in through bare feet

Correct. This head end with a hooked mouth is a hookworm's, such as Necator americanus. Humans shed eggs in feces, which hatch into filariform larvae that burrow into the skin of bare feet, travel by blood to the lungs, are swallowed, and mature and reproduce in the small intestine.
Swallowing eggs in food or water

Swallowing mature eggs in contaminated food or water is how Ascaris and the whipworm infect people. The worm with this hooked mouth, a hookworm, is infective in the larval stage: its filariform larvae burrow into the skin, on the soles of the feet.

set2.q: The worm pictured is being removed from a patient's eye. How do people acquire this worm?
opts: Eating undercooked fish

Inadequately cooked fish containing cercariae carry Opisthorchis sinensis, the Chinese liver fluke, whose larvae crawl into the bile duct. The worm drawn from the eye is Loa loa, the African eye worm, spread by the bite of small flies.
Larvae entering bare feet

Larvae burrowing into the skin of bare feet is how the hookworms infect, before they travel to the lungs, are swallowed and mature in the small intestine. The worm drawn from the eye is Loa loa, spread by the bite of small flies.
Eating raw aquatic plants

Raw aquatic plants carry Fasciola hepatica, a liver fluke that cycles between herbivores, snails and aquatic plants and lodges in the liver. The worm being pulled from the eye is Loa loa, the African eye worm, which reaches people through the bite of small flies.
The bite of small flies

Correct. A worm pulled from the eye is Loa loa, the African eye worm, spread by the bite of small flies. This temperature-sensitive worm migrates around and under the skin and may enter the eye, and treatment can be pulling the worm from a small hole in the conjunctiva.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Balantidium coli normally lives in the intestines of which animals?
opts: Domestic dogs

Dogs are the alternate hosts of Leishmania in equatorial regions, a blood and tissue parasite spread by female sand flies. Balantidium coli lives in the intestines of pigs and cattle and reaches humans in cyst-containing food or water.
House cats

Cats matter for Toxoplasma gondii (pregnant women should not clean the cat box) and are among the reservoirs of Giardia lamblia. Balantidium coli is the intestinal ciliate of domestic animals such as pigs and cattle.
Pigs and cattle

Correct. Balantidium coli, the intestinal ciliate, occupies the intestines of domestic animals such as pigs and cattle, its alternate hosts. Humans acquire it by ingesting cyst-containing food or water; the trophozoite erodes the intestine, but healthy humans are resistant.
Beavers and coyotes

Beavers and coyotes, with cattle, cats and humans, are reservoirs of Giardia lamblia, the heart-shaped flagellate swallowed with water and food. Balantidium coli is the intestinal ciliate of domestic animals, chiefly pigs and cattle.

set2.q: Which animal is the definitive host of the parasite that formed the cyst shown?
opts: Pigs

Pigs are intermediate hosts here, as swine are for the pork tapeworm, Taenia solium, whose definitive host is the human. Adulthood and mating occur in the definitive host, and for Echinococcus that host is the dog.
Dogs

Correct. The large cyst exposed at surgery is a hydatid cyst of Echinococcus, a tiny tapeworm whose definitive host is the dog, while sheep, cattle, goats and pigs are its intermediate hosts. Treatment often involves surgical removal of these parasitic masses.
Sheep

Sheep are intermediate hosts of Echinococcus, alongside cattle, goats and pigs. Adulthood and mating occur in the definitive host, and for this tiny tapeworm that host is the dog, which is also how people typically acquire it.
Cattle

Cattle are intermediate hosts of Echinococcus, and of the beef tapeworm, Taenia saginata, for which humans are the definitive host. The definitive host of Echinococcus, where adulthood and mating occur, is the dog.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: An acid-fast stained fecal smear from a patient with watery diarrhea, bloating and stomach cramps shows the round red-staining bodies seen here. Which parasite is it?
opts: Giardia lamblia

Giardia lamblia is recognized by its trophozoite's symmetrical heart shape, with a concave ventral surface that acts like a suction cup, and microscopy is difficult because it is shed intermittently. Round acid-fast-staining oocysts point to Cyclospora.
Entamoeba histolytica

Entamoeba histolytica is also sought in a fecal smear, but it shows a large trophozoite moving by pseudopods or a smaller nonmotile cyst, and it causes dysentery. Round oocysts staining with the acid-fast method are Cyclospora cayetanensis.
Balantidium coli

Balantidium coli is a ciliate from the intestines of pigs and cattle that causes persistent diarrhea and occasionally dysentery. The bodies in this acid-fast fecal smear are oocysts, the form of Cyclospora cayetanensis that invades the small intestinal mucosa.
Cyclospora cayetanensis

Correct. Round oocysts that take up the acid-fast stain in a fecal smear are Cyclospora cayetanensis, the cause of cyclosporiasis, with watery diarrhea, stomach cramps, bloating, fever and muscle aches. Diagnosis can be complicated, so multiple stool samples must be tested.

set2.q: What causes the massive swelling pictured, the result of a chronic tropical worm infection?
opts: Worms migrating under the skin

Migration around and under the skin, sometimes into the eye, is the behavior of Loa loa, the African eye worm. The massive limb swelling shown is elephantiasis, from adult filarial worms blocking lymphatic circulation.
Blocked lymphatic circulation

Correct. This is elephantiasis, massive swelling in the extremities from Bancroftian filariasis. Wuchereria bancrofti is spread by mosquitoes; the larvae they deposit move into the lymphatics and develop into adults, and chronic infection blocks lymphatic circulation.
Larvae encysted in the leg muscles

Larvae encysted in skeletal muscle are trichinellosis, from undercooked pork or bear meat, causing muscle and joint pain. Elephantiasis comes from filarial worms in the lymphatics blocking lymphatic circulation.
Inflammation from bacterial coinfection

Inflammation against antigens of the Wolbachia endosymbiont is how Onchocerca volvulus causes river blindness, damaging the cornea, retina and optic nerve. The swollen limbs of elephantiasis come from blocked lymphatic circulation.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Which list gives the effects of helminth pathology on the human host?
opts: Organ swelling, hemorrhage, weight loss, anemia

Correct. Worms feeding on and migrating through tissues, worms accumulating in organs and causing blockages, and toxic worm secretions produce enlargement and swelling of organs, hemorrhage, weight loss and anemia.
Specialized mouthparts, enzymes and a cuticle

Specialized mouthparts for attachment, enzymes to hydrolyze tissue and a cuticle for protection against immune defense are the worms' adaptations to parasitism, not effects on the host. The effects are enlargement and swelling of organs, hemorrhage, weight loss and anemia.
Eosinophilia, positive serology and eggs in feces

A raised eosinophil count, serological tests and eggs, larvae or adult worms in feces, sputum, urine, blood or tissue biopsies are the basis of diagnosis. The effects of helminth pathology are enlargement and swelling of organs, hemorrhage, weight loss and anemia.
Halted movement, lost grip and local gut action

Inhibiting the worm's movement, preventing it from holding its position and acting locally in the intestine describe what antihelminthic drugs do to the worm. Helminth pathology in the host shows as enlargement and swelling of organs, hemorrhage, weight loss and anemia.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Eggs like those pictured are identified in a specimen from a child. How is this worm typically spread?
opts: By close contact and fomites

Correct. These elongated eggs, flattened on one side, belong to the pinworm, Enterobius vermicularis. It is very common in daycare, with transmission by direct contact and fomites: eggs are picked up from the surroundings and swallowed, and self-inoculation is common. The tape test diagnoses it.
By fecal pollution of soil

Fecal pollution of soil with eggs spreads the whipworm and Ascaris, whose eggs are barrel-shaped with end plugs or broad ovals with a thick, rough shell. These flattened, elongated eggs are pinworm eggs, spread by close contact and fomites instead.
By larvae penetrating the feet

Larvae penetrating bare feet is the hookworm route, and hookworm eggs hatch in soil first. Pinworm eggs like these are infective as eggs, picked up from the surroundings or by self-inoculation and swallowed.
By eating undercooked pork

Undercooked pork or bear meat transmits Trichinella spiralis, whose larvae are encysted in the animal's muscle. The pinworm needs only humans; its eggs pass between people by close contact and fomites, and self-inoculation is common.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: What does visceral toxocariasis cause?
opts: Blocked lymphatic circulation

Blocked lymphatic circulation, leading to elephantiasis, is the work of Wuchereria bancrofti in the lymphatics. Visceral toxocariasis is migrating dog and cat roundworm larvae inflaming and severely damaging the liver.
Inflammation and severe liver damage

Correct. In toxocariasis, larvae of the dog and cat roundworms migrate through human tissues. Visceral toxocariasis brings inflammation and severe damage to the liver, while ocular toxocariasis, migration to the eye, may lead to visual impairment and total blindness.
Visual impairment and total blindness
Visual impairment and total blindness come from ocular toxocariasis, when larvae migrate to the eye. The visceral form is the one in the organs, with inflammation and severe damage to the liver.
Eosinophilic meningitis

Eosinophilic meningitis is caused by Angiostrongylus cantonensis, the rat lungworm, caught from snails, water or vegetables. Visceral toxocariasis, from dog and cat roundworm larvae, inflames and severely damages the liver.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Which genus of protozoa is shown in this stained blood smear?
opts: Trichomonas

Trichomonas is a small, pear-shaped flagellate of the urogenital tract, found on a vaginal smear, and it cannot survive long outside the host. Elongate flagellates among red blood cells in a blood smear are trypanosomes.
Trypanosoma

Correct. Elongate, spindle-shaped flagellates with tapered ends swimming between red blood cells are trypanosomes, readily demonstrated in blood, spinal fluid or lymph nodes. Trypanosoma brucei causes African sleeping sickness and Trypanosoma cruzi Chagas disease; both are hemoflagellates.
Plasmodium
Plasmodium is seen as small ring forms inside the red blood cells, not as long flagellates swimming between them. The thin, wavy cells lying outside the red cells in this smear are trypanosomes.
Leishmania

Leishmania multiplies inside human macrophages, which keep the infection localized or carry it systemically when they migrate. Free, spindle-shaped flagellates swimming between red blood cells, as here, are trypanosomes.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: What can treatment achieve once Trichinella spiralis larvae have encysted in muscle?
opts: It clears because larvae die quickly

Recovery because the parasite does not survive long in the human body is described for the rat lungworm, and only some of those patients recover. Trichinella cysts can remain in skeletal muscle for years, and there is no cure once larvae have encysted.
There is no cure at that point

Correct. Trichinellosis has no cure after the larvae have encysted. The larvae form cysts in muscle, heart and brain, and cysts in skeletal muscle can remain for years, after first symptoms of flulike illness and diarrhea and second symptoms of muscle and joint pain, shortness of breath and pronounced eosinophilia.
Surgical removal of the cysts cures it

Surgical removal of parasitic masses is used for Echinococcus, whose hydatid cysts may need to be surgically removed. Trichinella cysts form in muscle, heart and brain, and there is no cure once the larvae have encysted.
The worm can be pulled out intact

Pulling the worm out through a small hole in the conjunctiva treats Loa loa, the African eye worm, which migrates under the skin. Trichinella larvae lie encysted in muscle, heart and brain, and there is no cure once they have encysted.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set2.q: In the helminth life-cycle pattern whose intermediate host can be a biting insect, which stage infects the new human host?
opts: The second-stage larva

Correct. In this pattern the first larval stage infects the intermediate host, which then releases second-stage larvae. These are the infective form: they reach people from water or, when the intermediate host is a biting insect, through its bite, as with the filarial worms.
The first-stage larva

The first larval stage is the one that infects the intermediate host, after eggs are released into water with feces. It is the intermediate host's later product, the second-stage larva, that is infective for the next human.
The mature egg

Swallowing a mature egg in contaminated food or water is how the pattern without any intermediate host begins, as with Ascaris. When an intermediate host is involved, the human is infected by the second-stage larva it releases.
The larva encysted in muscle

Larvae encysted in muscle are what a person eats in undercooked meat, the pattern followed by Trichinella spiralis. In the pattern with an intermediate host, the infective form is the second-stage larva released into water or through a bite.

mis.The first-stage larva: first larval stage confused with the second

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set2.q: How are the hemoflagellates spread to humans?
opts: By sexual contact with carriers

Sexual contact spreads Trichomonas vaginalis, a flagellate of the urogenital tract rather than the blood. The hemoflagellates are vector-borne: blood-sucking insects serve as their intermediate hosts.
By blood-sucking insects

Correct. Hemoflagellates are obligate parasites of human blood and tissues, spread in specific tropical regions by blood-sucking insects that serve as intermediate hosts: the tsetse fly for Trypanosoma brucei, the reduviid bug for Trypanosoma cruzi and the female sand fly for Leishmania.
By swallowed cysts in water

Swallowed cysts are the fecal-oral route of the intestinal protozoa: Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia lamblia and Balantidium coli. Hemoflagellates live in blood and tissues and are zoonoses spread by blood-sucking insects that serve as intermediate hosts.
By nasal contact with water

Nasal contact with water is how the free-living ameba Naegleria fowleri reaches the brain along the olfactory nerve. Hemoflagellates are vector-borne blood parasites, carried by blood-sucking insects that act as intermediate hosts.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Which life-cycle forms does Trichomonas have?
opts: Cyst only

Trichomonas never forms a cyst; it exists only as the trophozoite, the active feeding cell by whose simple asexual division most protozoa propagate. Cysts belong to the cycles of Entamoeba, Giardia and Balantidium.
Trophozoite and cyst

Alternating between a motile trophozoite and a cyst is the cycle of Entamoeba histolytica (large trophozoite, smaller nonmotile cyst) and of Giardia lamblia. Trichomonas exists only in trophozoite form, with no cyst.
Sexual and asexual stages

Alternating between sexual and asexual phases is the complex life cycle of the apicomplexan parasites, such as Plasmodium and Toxoplasma. Trichomonas propagates as the trophozoite alone and never forms a cyst.
Trophozoite only

Correct. Trichomonads are small, pear-shaped flagellates with anterior flagella and an undulating membrane that exist only in trophozoite form; there is no cyst. Trichomonas vaginalis is also a strict parasite that cannot survive long outside the host.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Why is Chagas disease becoming more of an issue in the southern United States?
opts: Imported produce is contaminated

Water and fresh produce are the sources of Cyclospora cayetanensis, an intestinal protozoan. Trypanosoma cruzi reaches people through the feces of the reduviid bug, and its rise in the southern United States comes from vector migration.
Sexual spread is increasing

Sexual spread belongs to Trichomonas vaginalis, whose trichomoniasis is a sexually transmitted disease. Chagas disease is vector-borne; it is becoming an issue in the southern United States because the reduviid bug vector is expanding its range.
Its vector is migrating there

Correct. Chagas disease (American trypanosomiasis) has millions of cases in Latin America but is becoming more of an issue in the southern United States through vector migration: the reduviid (kissing) bug is expanding its range. Many now consider it endemic in the United States, and control is through control of the vector.
Freshwater lakes are warming

Lakes, streams and hot springs are the home of the free-living ameba Naegleria fowleri, acquired through the nose. Chagas disease is insect-borne, and it is rising in the southern United States because its vector, the reduviid bug, is migrating there.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Which vector carries Babesia microti, the cause of human babesiosis?
opts: Female Anopheles mosquito

The female Anopheles mosquito carries Plasmodium, which also invades red blood cells and causes anemia, so the two are easy to confuse. Babesia microti is carried by the blacklegged deer tick, and Babesia was the first protozoan linked to a vector at all.
Reduviid (kissing) bug

The reduviid or kissing bug is the vector of Trypanosoma cruzi and Chagas disease, which is becoming more of an issue in the southern United States as the vector migrates. Babesia microti reaches people through the blacklegged deer tick.
Female sand fly

Female sand flies, which need a blood meal to make eggs, transmit Leishmania among mammals, with dogs as alternate hosts. Babesiosis is a tick-borne zoonosis: Babesia microti is carried by the blacklegged deer tick and attacks red blood cells.
Blacklegged deer tick

Correct. Human babesiosis is caused by Babesia microti carried by the blacklegged deer tick; Babesia was the first protozoan found to be associated with a vector, the tick. The parasite attacks red blood cells and can cause hemolytic anemia; babesiosis is serious for people without a spleen.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: What can Cryptosporidium cause in a patient with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome?
opts: Severe hemolytic anemia

Hemolytic anemia results when Babesia microti, carried by the blacklegged deer tick, attacks red blood cells, and babesiosis is serious in the immunocompromised. Cryptosporidium invades intestinal cells instead, causing chronic persistent diarrhea in these patients.
Cyclic chills, fever and sweating

Regular episodes of chills, fever and sweating come from Plasmodium as red blood cells rupture in malaria. Cryptosporidium is an intestinal pathogen; in acquired immunodeficiency syndrome it may cause chronic persistent diarrhea.
Chronic persistent diarrhea

Correct. Cryptosporidium is an intestinal pathogen: swallowed oocysts release sporozoites that penetrate intestinal cells and cause gastroenteritis. Patients with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome and other immunocompromised hosts may suffer chronic persistent diarrhea, and few drugs are effective against it.
Encephalitis with brain damage

Brain and heart damage, Toxoplasma encephalitis, is the serious complication of toxoplasmosis in immunocompromised individuals. Cryptosporidium is an intestinal pathogen, and in acquired immunodeficiency syndrome its danger is chronic persistent diarrhea.
set2.cite: Lecture 16 Dr. Webster Parasites of Medical Importance.pptx, Slide 72, 73, 64, 77 and 60

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Where do adult schistosomes live and feed on blood?
opts: Bile ducts draining the liver

The bile duct is where the larvae of the Chinese liver fluke, Opisthorchis sinensis, mature and shed eggs into the feces. Young schistosomes do mature in the liver, but the adults then move on to the veins of the bowel or bladder to feed on blood.
The lungs, causing an abscess

Migration to the lungs, with cough, pleural pain and abscess, marks the lung fluke, Paragonimus westermani. Schistosomiasis can bring a cough, yet its adults live in the veins of the bowel or bladder and shed eggs into urine and feces.
Cysts in heart muscle or eye

Cysts in heart muscle, eye or brain are the encysted larvae of the pork tapeworm in cysticercosis. Adult schistosomes are not encysted: they are paired blood flukes feeding on blood in the veins of the bowel or bladder.
Veins of the bowel or bladder

Correct. Schistosomes are blood flukes: after maturing in the liver, the adults migrate to the intestine or bladder, feed on blood and shed eggs into urine and feces. The paired adults sit in the mesenteric venules of the bowel or rectum, or in the venous plexus of the bladder.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set2.q: How do humans acquire Fasciola hepatica?
opts: Eating raw aquatic plants

Correct. Fasciola hepatica, the sheep liver fluke, cycles between herbivores such as sheep and cattle, snails, and aquatic plants. Humans are infected by eating raw aquatic plants (water plants), after which the fluke lodges in the liver.
Eating undercooked fish

Inadequately cooked freshwater fish transmit the Chinese liver fluke, Opisthorchis sinensis, the reason for the warning against freshwater sushi. Fasciola hepatica reaches humans on raw aquatic plants, the third host in its cycle with herbivores and snails.
Eating undercooked crabs

Undercooked crabs and other crustaceans transmit the lung fluke, Paragonimus westermani. Fasciola hepatica cycles between herbivores, snails and aquatic plants, so humans catch it by eating the plants raw.
Eating raw or undercooked beef

Raw beef in which the larval form has encysted transmits the beef tapeworm, Taenia saginata. Cattle are herbivore hosts of Fasciola hepatica too, but humans acquire this fluke by eating raw aquatic plants, not beef.

mis.Eating raw or undercooked beef: herbivore host mistaken for the human source

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set2.q: How do humans acquire Ascaris lumbricoides?
opts: Eating undercooked pork holding larval cysts

Undercooked pork or bear meat carries Trichinella spiralis larvae encysted in muscle. Ascaris is indigenous to humans, with no food animal in its cycle; its eggs pass in feces and are swallowed in food, drink or on contaminated objects.
Eating raw snails or contaminated produce

Raw snails and contaminated water or vegetables transmit Angiostrongylus cantonensis, the rat lungworm, whose intermediate hosts are snails. Ascaris needs no intermediate host: its eggs pass from one person's feces to another person in food, drink or on objects.
Swallowing eggs in food, drink or on objects

Correct. Ascaris spends its larval and adult stages in humans and releases embryonic eggs in feces; they spread to other people in food, drink or on contaminated objects. Swallowed eggs hatch, and the larvae travel through the circulation to the lungs and pharynx and are swallowed to mature in the intestine.
Larvae burrowing into the skin of bare feet

Larvae that burrow into the skin of bare feet are how hookworms infect people; their eggs hatch in soil into filariform larvae. Ascaris is infective in the egg stage instead, so it is swallowed rather than entering through the skin.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: How does the number of antiprotozoan drugs compare with the number of antibacterial agents?
opts: Relatively few

Correct. Antiprotozoan drugs are relatively few in comparison with antibacterial agents. Protozoa are single-celled, animal-like eukaryotic parasites, so these drugs must work against eukaryotic cells, and they bring toxicity problems and severe side effects as well.
About as many

The two groups are not matched in size: antiprotozoan drugs are relatively few in comparison with antibacterial agents. What sets them apart is that they work against eukaryotic cells, the cell type of protozoa, and carry toxicity problems and severe side effects.
Somewhat more

Antiprotozoan drugs do not outnumber antibacterial agents at all; they are relatively few by comparison. Their other defining features are that they work against eukaryotic cells and have toxicity problems with severe side effects.
Many more

This reverses the comparison: antibacterial agents are the larger group, and antiprotozoan drugs are relatively few beside them. Antiprotozoan drugs also work against eukaryotic cells and carry toxicity problems and severe side effects.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Amebiasis epidemics sometimes occur in prisons, hospitals and juvenile care institutions. Which shared condition explains these outbreaks?
opts: Insects biting the residents

Biting insects spread the hemoflagellates (Trypanosoma and Leishmania), blood parasites with insect intermediate hosts. Entamoeba histolytica is intestinal and fecal-oral, so outbreaks in crowded institutions come from polluted water supplies.
Polluted water supplies

Correct. Epidemics of amebiasis sometimes occur in concentrated populations where water supplies are polluted, such as prisons, hospitals and juvenile care institutions. The cysts are swallowed with contaminated water or food (the fecal-oral route), and prevention rests on water treatment.
Unchlorinated swimming pools

Unchlorinated swimming pools, hot springs, lakes and streams hold the free-living amebas Naegleria and Acanthamoeba, which enter through the nose, eye or broken skin. Institutional outbreaks of amebiasis come from polluted water supplies that people swallow.
Contact with pigs and cattle

Pigs and cattle are the hosts of Balantidium coli, the intestinal ciliate. Entamoeba histolytica has humans as its primary hosts, and its institutional outbreaks trace to polluted water supplies in crowded populations.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: A woman acquires toxoplasmosis during pregnancy, and the parasite crosses the placenta. Which findings may her newborn show?
opts: Eyelid swelling with conjunctivitis and fever

A swelling of the eyelid with conjunctivitis (Romana's sign), with fever, marks Chagas disease from Trypanosoma cruzi, which can also be transmitted congenitally. Congenital toxoplasmosis brings hydrocephalus, intracranial calcifications and chorioretinitis.
Anemia with an enlarged spleen and liver

Anemia and enlargement of the spleen, liver and kidneys are complications of malaria, and Plasmodium can also pass from mother to fetus. The newborn findings of toxoplasmosis acquired across the placenta are hydrocephalus, intracranial calcifications and chorioretinitis.
Personality changes and sleep disturbances

Personality and behavioral changes progressing to sleep disturbances belong to African sleeping sickness, once Trypanosoma brucei reaches the central nervous system after a tsetse fly bite. Toxoplasmosis passed across the placenta gives hydrocephalus and intracranial calcifications.
Hydrocephalus and intracranial calcifications

Correct. Transplacental transmission from a pregnant woman with toxoplasmosis can cause spontaneous abortion, stillbirth, or severe neurological and ocular manifestations in the newborn, including hydrocephalus, intracranial calcifications and chorioretinitis. Hence pregnant women should not clean the cat box.

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Which Plasmodium species causes the most malignant malaria, with the highest death rate in children?
opts: Plasmodium vivax

Plasmodium vivax is another malaria species spread by the female Anopheles mosquito, but it is not the one singled out as the most malignant. That is Plasmodium falciparum, which also carries the highest death rate in children.
Plasmodium malariae

Plasmodium malariae causes malaria with the same chills-fever-sweating episodes as red blood cells rupture, but it is not named the most malignant type. Plasmodium falciparum holds that place, with the highest death rate in children.
Plasmodium ovale

Plasmodium ovale is named among the species that cause malaria, but it is not the malignant one. The most malignant type, with the highest death rate in children, is Plasmodium falciparum; the other species differ in the interval between episodes.
Plasmodium falciparum

Correct. Plasmodium falciparum is the most malignant type of malaria and has the highest death rate in children. The malaria species share the regular episodes of chills, fever and sweating as red blood cells rupture, though the interval between episodes depends on the species.
set2.cite: Lecture 16 Dr. Webster Parasites of Medical Importance.pptx, Slide 56 and 60

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Which insect spreads Trypanosoma brucei, the cause of African sleeping sickness?
opts: The tsetse fly

Correct. African sleeping sickness is spread by tsetse flies and harbored by reservoir mammals. The fly's bite inoculates the skin, where a primary chancre develops, and the parasite spreads through the lymphatics and blood; control involves eliminating the tsetse fly.
The female sand fly
Female sand flies, which need a blood meal to produce eggs, transmit Leishmania with their bite. Trypanosoma brucei uses a different insect, the tsetse fly of West and East Africa.
The reduviid bug

The reduviid (kissing) bug is the vector of Trypanosoma cruzi, which causes Chagas disease (American trypanosomiasis) through infected bug feces. The African trypanosome, Trypanosoma brucei, is spread by the tsetse fly.
The Anopheles mosquito

The Anopheles mosquito is the vector of Plasmodium, the cause of malaria, seen as ring forms inside red blood cells. Trypanosoma brucei is spread by tsetse flies, and control involves eliminating them.
