set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: After Plasmodium sporozoites enter a capillary with the vector's saliva, where do they localize first?
opts: The liver

Correct. The injected sporozoite localizes in the liver, invades liver cells and undergoes schizogony, generating numerous merozoites; this is the exoerythrocytic phase. Only afterward do the merozoites enter the circulation and invade red blood cells (the erythrocytic phase).
Red blood cells

Red blood cells are the second stop, not the first: merozoites released from the liver attach to and enter them, become ring trophozoites and multiply in the erythrocytic phase. The sporozoite itself goes first to the liver for schizogony.
The intestinal lining

Penetrating intestinal cells is what Cryptosporidium sporozoites do after swallowed oocysts release them. Plasmodium sporozoites arrive in the blood, not the gut, and localize first in the liver, where schizogony produces merozoites.
The spleen

Enlargement of the spleen, liver and kidneys is a complication of malaria, not the sporozoite's first stop. The sporozoite invades liver cells and divides there, releasing large numbers of merozoites into the circulation.

mis.The spleen: complication mistaken for the first stage

set2.cite: Lecture 16 Dr. Webster Parasites of Medical Importance.pptx, Slide 58, 59, 60 and 73

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Which event defines a helminth's definitive host?
opts: Development of the larval stages

Larval development is what defines the intermediate host, not the definitive host. In the pattern that involves an intermediate host, the first larval stage infects it, and it later releases the infective second-stage larvae. Adulthood and mating define the definitive host.
Carrying the worm without development

A host in which the worm experiences no parasitic development is a transport host, such as the waterfowl whose undercooked meat can pass Toxocara on. The definitive host is the opposite case: there the worms grow to adults and mate.
Release of second-stage larvae into water

Releasing infective second-stage larvae into water, or passing them on through a bite, is the job of the intermediate host in the pattern that needs one. The definitive host is where the worms end up as adults that mate and make eggs.
Adulthood and mating of the worms

Correct. Adulthood and mating occur in the definitive host. There the adult worms mate and produce fertilized eggs that hatch, and the larvae then mature in several stages. For Toxocara canis and cati, for example, the adults live in the small intestine of the dog or cat, the definitive host.
set2.cite: Lecture 16 Dr. Webster Parasites of Medical Importance.pptx, Slide 79, 83, 108 and 109

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Which group accounts for most cases of Naegleria fowleri meningoencephalitis?
opts: Children and young adults

Correct. Most cases of Naegleria meningoencephalitis occur in children and young adults, through exposure to freshwater lakes and streams while diving, waterskiing or jet skiing. Water reaching the nose carries the trophozoites, which travel to the brain through the olfactory nerve.
Contact lens wearers

Contact lens wearers are the risk group for amebic keratitis caused by Acanthamoeba, with eye pain, redness and irritation. Naegleria meningoencephalitis strikes mostly children and young adults exposed to freshwater lakes and streams.
Immunocompromised adults

Compromised immune systems set the stage for Acanthamoeba's granulomatous amebic encephalitis and disseminated disease. Naegleria fowleri mainly affects children and young adults who are exposed to fresh water.
Young, sexually active women

Young, sexually active women are the group in which trichomoniasis is the most common curable sexually transmitted disease. Naegleria is acquired from water, and most cases are children and young adults exposed to freshwater lakes and streams.
set2.cite: Lecture 16 Dr. Webster Parasites of Medical Importance.pptx, Slide 28, 29, 31, 32 and 37

set2.io: 2 — Describe the modes of transmission by which humans acquire parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Amebic keratitis caused by Acanthamoeba occurs mainly in which group?
opts: Young, sexually active women

Young, sexually active women are the group in which trichomoniasis is the most common curable sexually transmitted disease. Amebic keratitis is an eye infection from Acanthamoeba that occurs in contact lens wearers.
Campers

Campers are the group in whom giardiasis is common, from Giardia lamblia cysts swallowed with water or food (its reservoirs include beavers and coyotes). Acanthamoeba keratitis, with eye pain, redness and irritation, occurs in contact lens wearers.
Contact lens wearers

Correct. Acanthamoeba, distributed worldwide in freshwater lakes, hot tubs and swimming pools, causes amebic keratitis in contact lens wearers, with eye pain, redness and irritation. The eye infection does not typically disseminate, unlike its granulomatous amebic encephalitis.
Children and young adults

Children and young adults exposed to freshwater lakes and streams make up most cases of Naegleria meningoencephalitis, a brain infection. Acanthamoeba keratitis, an eye infection with pain, redness and irritation, is linked to contact lens wearers.
set2.cite: Lecture 16 Dr. Webster Parasites of Medical Importance.pptx, Slide 4, 28, 31, 37 and 39

set2.io: 1 — Compare and contrast the morphology, medium, laboratory tests, biochemical reactions, diseases, clinical manifestations, methods of treatment, and prevention of parasites of medical importance
set2.q: Which disease does this brain scan show?
opts: Taeniasis

Taeniasis is the intestinal form: cysts eaten in meat release larvae that develop into tapeworms attached to the intestine. Tissue cysts such as these in the brain mean the eggs were swallowed, and that causes cysticercosis instead.
Schistosomiasis

Schistosomiasis is a blood fluke disease that enlarges and inflames the liver, spleen and bladder. Many small cysts throughout the brain point instead to cysticercosis, the encysted larvae of the pork tapeworm.
Cysticercosis

Correct. Countless small cysts scattered through the brain are neurocysticercosis: swallowed pork tapeworm eggs hatch and release larvae that migrate to all tissues and encyst. Cysts in the brain are among the most damaging and may cause seizures and psychiatric disturbances.
Hydatid disease

Hydatid disease (cystic echinococcosis) forms slowly enlarging cysts in the liver and lungs, from a tiny tapeworm found in dogs. The scan instead shows many small cysts spread through the brain, the picture of cysticercosis from the pork tapeworm.

mis.Taeniasis: intestinal form confused with the tissue form
mis.Schistosomiasis: fluke disease confused with tapeworm cysts
